title: Codex users question a persistent, self-updating background daemon
friendlyTitle: Codex CLI may keep a background service running
summary: A widely discussed Codex issue says CLI version 0.157.0 can start a persistent app-server daemon, copy its package into a separate release directory and run an hourly update loop. The open request asks OpenAI to make automatic startup opt-in; it also documents a command for disabling the feature.
friendlySummary: A GitHub report says a recent Codex CLI version starts a service that can stay open and update itself after the main window closes.
whyItMatters: Developer tools that remain running or update outside the package manager affect security, reproducibility and network policy. Codex CLI users should review the issue, inspect their local process behavior and choose whether the convenience fits their environment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Developers should know what keeps running on their computers and decide whether automatic updates are suitable for their work.
